export ui-component Planning:
    pitch:
        A plain, quick list of the work still to do, as Linear keeps issues:
        stories written ahead of time, each saying how it will be sent, Code,
        Chain, Spec, Ask, or Freeform, gathered into the next sprint and sent
        to the agent in order, all at once.

    description:
        Planning opens in a tab of its own in the body, "Planning", with a
        checklist icon, as a file opens, as the @{Body} says, from the
        ribbon's Planning tab or the palette's "Planning". It is one column
        of stories, at most 760 pixels wide, centred, in sections, each
        headed by its name and count: "Current sprint", at the top, only
        while a sprint is under way, then "Next sprint", and "Backlog"
        beneath them. A section with nothing in it reads, muted,
        "Nothing planned" or "Backlog is empty".

    stories:
        A story is one piece of work, written as it will be sent: a title,
        a prompt, and how it will be sent. Each is a row, 36 pixels tall: a
        drag grip at its left; a small mode picker, a pill reading its mode,
        "Code", "Chain", "Spec", "Ask", or "Freeform", in that mode's colour,
        as the @{PromptModes} colours it; its title, in the body's text
        colour, cut off with an ellipsis; then, at its right, muted, a small
        icon for anything attached, and, once it has been sent, its status
        as a task's is shown. Hovering a row shows a menu button at its
        right. A story has no Send of its own, as the sprint says.

        Clicking a row opens it beneath, expanded in place, the others
        moving down: its title, editable in place; its prompt, in a
        @{GrowingTextInput} with the chat input's highlighting, completions,
        and slicing, as the @{ChatInput} has, and its attachments beneath;
        and its parameters, its mode, model, effort, and Slice, as the chat
        input shows them. Every change is saved as it is made. Only one
        story is open at a time; Escape or clicking its row again closes
        it.

    creating:
        Creating a story is quick. A "New story" line at the foot of Next
        sprint, and Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS) while Planning has focus, adds a
        story at the end of Next sprint, open, its title focused, in the mode
        last picked for a story. However a story is added, it goes into Next
        sprint, at its end: a new story, a duplicate, and one added from an
        Ask answer's card with "Add to sprint" alike. It can then be moved to
        the Backlog to wait, as the sprint says. The one exception is an
        accepted proposal for a new story, from drafting, research, or an
        Ask answer's proposal card, which goes into the Backlog, at its end,
        as the proposal cards say, and reaches a sprint only once it is
        moved to Next sprint. Typing a title and pressing Enter adds it and starts another
        beneath it, so a list can be written down without the mouse; Escape
        on an empty one removes it. A title with no prompt sends its title as
        its prompt.

        A story can also be prompted into existence: "Draft stories", a
        button beside the Backlog's heading, opens a small box to say what is
        wanted, in a sentence or a paragraph, and asks the harness, in a run
        of its own with no session, with the planning prompt of the
        @{BakedSystemPrompts}, to break it into stories, each with a title, a
        prompt, and the mode that fits it. They come back as proposals, as
        the drafting and proposals say, each to be accepted, edited, or
        rejected, and none reaches the plan until it is accepted. An Ask
        answer's prompt cards also offer "Add to sprint", which adds the
        card's prompt as a story in its mode to Next sprint.

    sprint:
        Stories move between the Backlog and Next sprint by dragging, as the
        @{DragReorderBehaviour} says, across the sections as within them, or
        from a row's menu, "Move to next sprint" or "Move to backlog". Their
        order within Next sprint is the order they will be sent. A row's menu
        also has "Duplicate" and "Delete".

        "Send sprint", a primary button at the right of Next sprint's
        heading, enabled while it holds a story, sends every story in it, in
        order, as though each had been written in the chat input on its
        mode's tab and sent, one after another, as the @{PromptSending} says:
        each task queues in its lane behind the one before it, in the order
        of the sprint, and each question runs at once. The stories go into
        the queue as one block, so nothing sent later comes between them,
        and the queue's auto-send carries them on as ever, as the
        @{QueueList} says.

        A story can't be sent on its own. The only way a story reaches work
        is through the sprint: a story in the Backlog waits until it is
        moved into Next sprint and the sprint is sent, and a story in Next
        sprint goes when the sprint does. Nothing in Planning, its rows,
        their menus, the open story, the keyboard, the palette, or the
        ribbon, sends a single story, and nothing elsewhere sends a story by
        any other route: a story can't be dragged or copied into the chat
        input or the queue to be sent from there, and its menu has no "Send"
        or "Edit in chat input". The chat input's own prompts are not
        stories and are sent as ever; once a prompt is a story, the sprint is
        its only way to work. To send one story at once, it is the only story in
        Next sprint when Send sprint is pressed. A story that failed or was
        cancelled is sent again the same way, with the next sprint.

        Sending the sprint moves its stories into a "Current sprint" section,
        above Next sprint, shown only while it holds a story, so Next sprint
        is empty again and stories added meanwhile go there, to be the
        sprint after. A story in Current sprint keeps its place, its row
        showing its task's status as it queues, runs, and ends, and clicking
        it opens its task in the Tasks tab; it can't be moved or edited
        there. Once every story of Current sprint has ended, the section
        offers "Close sprint", which moves the stories that are done into a
        muted, collapsed "Done" list beneath the Backlog, and those that
        failed, were cancelled, or stopped to the start of Next sprint, in
        their order, to be sent again. While a sprint is current, Send sprint
        is disabled, its tooltip saying a sprint is already under way.

        Send sprint only ever moves into Current sprint the stories it
        actually sent. A story with nothing to send, its title and its prompt
        both empty, is skipped: it stays in Next sprint, where it was, and
        Send sprint's result says, muted, how many it skipped and why, as "1
        empty story left in Next sprint". A sprint where every story is
        empty sends nothing and makes no Current sprint.

        Once a sprint is done, it can always be closed. Every story of
        Current sprint counts as ended once its task has ended, done,
        failed, cancelled, or stopped, or once its task can no longer be
        found, as when its record was deleted, it was never recorded, or the
        application quit before it was. A story whose task is missing is
        never shown as Queued, or as anything still to come: its row reads
        "Task missing", muted, in the theme's warning colour, its tooltip
        saying its task can't be found, and it counts as ended and not Done.
        A story still waiting in its lane's queue, or held for review, as
        the paused section says, is still to come and hasn't ended. So Close
        sprint shows as soon as no story of Current sprint is building,
        compiling, running, paused, queued, or held, and never waits on a
        task that can't arrive.

        Close sprint treats a story whose task is missing as it treats one
        that failed or was cancelled: it goes back to the start of Next
        sprint, with the others sent again, in their order, never into Done.
        Closing saves the sections, Done, Next sprint, the Backlog, and
        the emptied Current sprint, to `order.json` straight away, as the
        @{ProjectData} says, and Current sprint's state is worked out afresh
        from the stories' tasks whenever the plan is read, so a sprint that
        finished, or whose tasks went missing, before a reload or a restart
        can still be closed after it, as before.

    autoStart:
        Next sprint can start on its own: a "Start automatically" switch on
        Next sprint's heading, beside Send sprint, its tooltip saying the
        next sprint starts as soon as the current one is done. It starts
        off, and is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, so it is kept
        across reloads and restarts.

        While it is on, once every story of Current sprint has ended Done,
        the current sprint closes by itself, as Close sprint closes it, and
        Next sprint, if it holds a story, is sent at once, as Send sprint
        sends it, with nobody having to start it; and while no sprint is
        current, a story added to an empty Next sprint starts it the same
        way. A sprint that ended with a story failed, cancelled, stopped, or with its task missing,
        never starts the next by itself: it waits, Close sprint offered as
        ever, and the switch's row says, in the theme's warning colour, why
        the next didn't start. Nor does the next start while planning is
        paused, as the paused section says: it starts once the pause is
        ended by Resume, or Approve, if the switch is still on. An empty Next
        sprint starts nothing.

        Each time a sprint starts by itself, a passive notification says
        so, "Next sprint started: 4 stories", with a link that opens
        Planning, and the debug log records it. Turning the switch off
        never stops a sprint already sent; it only keeps the next from
        starting by itself. Turning it on while no sprint is current and
        Next sprint holds a story starts Next sprint at once, as adding a
        story to it would, unless planning is paused.

        The switch works while Planning isn't open, from the plan as saved,
        whichever tab is shown. When the project is opened, or the
        application starts, with the switch on, no sprint current, and Next
        sprint holding a story, it doesn't start by itself; the switch's row
        says, muted, "Waiting to start", with a "Start now" button, so a
        sprint never begins unseen as the application opens. A current
        sprint whose stories were cut off when the application quit, as
        every run is, ended them, and never starts the next by itself.

        While the switch is on, Next sprint's heading shows "Auto" beside
        its count, in the theme's accent, and the ribbon's Send Sprint
        button's tooltip says the next sprint starts automatically.

    saving:
        The stories, their order, and which section each is in are saved
        with the project's data, as the @{ProjectData} says, in
        `.suspense/planning/`, a file per story, holding its hidden anchor
        as a queued prompt's is, and an `order.json` listing the sections and
        their stories, so the plan is kept with the project and comes back
        as it was left. A story's steps are saved in its own file, in their
        order, as its steps say, never apart from it.

    steps:
        A story can have steps: one or more further prompts, each a piece of
        the story done after the one before, as a chain's steps are. Each
        step has a prompt, a mode of its own, Code or Spec, starting as the
        story's, and a model and effort, starting as the story's, and may
        have attachments. A story with no steps is just its own prompt, as
        before; its prompt is always its first step.

        An open story lists its steps beneath its prompt, in order, each a
        row numbered from 2, the story's own prompt being 1, with its mode
        pill and the first line of its prompt, opening in place to edit, as
        a story does. "Add step", beneath the last, adds one at the end,
        open and focused; several can be added one after another, Enter in
        an empty step's prompt adding none. Steps are reordered by dragging,
        as the @{DragReorderBehaviour} says, or Alt+Up and Alt+Down, and each
        has a remove button in its row and in its menu. The story's own
        prompt stays first and can't be moved among them.

        A step belongs to its story and to nothing else. It is saved in the
        story's file, in a `steps` list of the story's hidden anchor, in its
        order, and saved as every change to the plan is, straight away; a
        story duplicated copies its steps, and one deleted deletes them. Its
        order is kept wherever the story goes, between sections, into a
        sprint, and back from Done.

        Wherever the story is shown, its steps are too: its row in Planning
        shows how many after its title, muted, as "3 steps", with the list in
        its tooltip; the open story lists them as above; a proposal to add
        to it shows them, so what it would add to can be seen; and once it
        is sent, it is sent as a chain, its prompt first and each step after
        it in order, each step sent only once the one before it finishes, as
        the @{PromptEditor}'s chained tasks are, so the Tasks tab shows the
        story as one chain with its steps beneath it. A story sent can't be
        given more steps; its steps, sent or still to come, read as they
        were sent. In Current sprint, a story with steps is expanded, a row
        for each step beneath it, in order, indented 16 pixels, each with its
        own status, as a running chain's are in the Tasks tab; in Done, and
        in a finding started from the story, its steps are listed the same
        way, collapsed to its step count until it is expanded. The same steps,
        in the same order, are what every place shows, since every place
        reads them from the story's own file.

        A step is only ever added to a story that exists. Adding one to a
        story that doesn't, as one deleted while a proposal naming it waited,
        or by another window, or whose file was removed from
        `.suspense/planning/` meanwhile, changes nothing: no story is made
        for it, no other story is given it, and nothing is saved. It says so
        in plain words where it was asked for, as "That story no longer
        exists, so the step wasn't added", in the theme's error colour, as
        the states say, with what was to be added kept, so it can be added
        to another story or as a new one. A step added to a story already
        sent is refused the same way, saying the story has been sent.

    layout:
        Everything in Planning is laid out on one rhythm, so it scans as a
        single list. The column has 24 pixels of padding at its top and
        sides. Each section's heading is a row 32 pixels tall: its name in
        small semibold text, its count beside it, muted, and its actions at
        its right, each a labelled button, never an icon alone; 8 pixels
        beneath it its first row. Story rows are 36 pixels tall, 2 pixels
        apart, each with 12 pixels of padding at either side, their parts in
        fixed columns, so the grips, mode pills, titles, and statuses line up
        down the whole list: the grip 16 pixels, the mode pill 72 pixels, the
        title the rest, the status and time right-aligned in a column of
        their own 96 pixels wide, then the row's buttons. Sections are 24
        pixels apart. Every row's state reads the same way, as below, and
        every label is the same small text, muted where it is secondary.

        From top to bottom, Planning reads: the pause bar, while paused;
        Current sprint, while a sprint is under way; Next sprint; Backlog;
        Findings; and Done, collapsed. Each is a section headed as above, so
        nothing sits outside the rhythm, and an open story, a drafting or
        research panel, and the citations and steps inside a story all use
        the same three parts, below.

    parts:
        Everything in Planning is built from three parts, each always drawn
        the same way:

        \\
        - A row: 36 pixels tall, in the fixed columns above, for stories, steps, findings, and Done; its secondary text muted and cut off with an ellipsis, its buttons small ghost buttons with labels, shown at its right on hover and always while it is focused
        - A panel: an inset area 16 pixels below what opened it, on the theme's raised surface, corners rounded 6 pixels, 12 pixels of padding, a heading row of 32 pixels with its name, as "Draft stories", "Research", or the story's title, and its close button, its content beneath, and its actions in a footer row, right-aligned, the primary action last; used for an open story, drafting, and research
        - A card: a box inside a panel, on the theme's base surface, with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour, corners rounded 4 pixels, 12 pixels of padding, 8 pixels from the next; a label row at its top, its content, and a footer row of labelled buttons; used for proposals and for each finding's summary
        \\

        Labels are words, never icons alone: every button reads what it
        does, "Accept", "Send sprint", "Start automatically", and an icon
        beside a label only repeats it. Each heading's count is a plain
        number, muted, and each status a coloured label, as the states say.
        The pause bar is a row across the column's top, 40 pixels tall, its
        text and buttons on one line, the same height whatever it says.

    states:
        Each part of Planning has the same few states, shown the same way
        wherever they come up, so a state is never guessed from what is
        missing.

        \\
        - Empty: a single muted line, centred in the section, saying what is missing and what to do, as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N.", with no illustration
        - Loading: a spinner and a short muted label of what is happening, as "Drafting stories…", in the place the result will appear, never a blank space
        - Paused: a story whose task is paused shows "Paused" as its status, in the theme's warning colour, with a small pause icon, and a "Resume" button in its row, as the PromptSending says of pausing; a sprint with any story paused says so in its heading, as "1 paused", in the same colour
        - Error: a line in the theme's error colour, saying what went wrong in plain words, with what the harness or the application reported beneath it collapsed under "Details", and a "Try again" button where trying again can help
        \\

        A story's status in its row is the same coloured label a task has,
        as the @{MessageList}'s status says, Queued, Running with its spinner
        and time, Done, Failed, Cancelled, Paused, or, where its task can't be found, Task missing, as the sprint says, and a story not yet
        sent shows nothing there, so its absence means "not sent".

        Each part shows each state that can come up for it, worded for it:

        \\
        - Story list: empty, "Nothing planned. Press Ctrl+N to add a story." in Next sprint and "Nothing waiting." in the Backlog; loading, while the plan is read on opening, a row of skeleton rows, never an empty section; error, when the plan can't be read or saved, saying which file and why, with "Try again"
        - Research and its findings: loading, the live line of what it is reading with its spinner; empty, "No findings yet." in Findings; error, the run's failure with "Try again", which keeps the question in its box; a finding that ended early, as stopped, marked "Incomplete", muted, in its row
        - Pause: the pause bar, in the theme's warning colour, as the paused section says, and the sprint's Send buttons disabled with their tooltips saying why; a sprint that can't start for a failed story says so in its heading, in the same colour
        - Proposals: loading, the drafting line and spinner; empty, "No stories proposed." with "Draft again"; error, the run's failure with "Try again"; a proposal with no spec cited, in the warning colour with "Draft again", as the spec grounding says
        \\

    drafting:
        Drafting stories shows its work in one place, a panel opened beneath
        the Backlog's heading, never in a popup that hides the list. It has
        the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and
        beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what
        the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner,
        updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel
        lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all"
        buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left
        to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and
        leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing
        says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided,
        so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.

        Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent"
        in its row's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then
        reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's
        title and prompt, and the panel opens beneath that story rather than
        the Backlog's heading.

    proposals:
        The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run,
        as the @{Sandbox} says, able to read the project and change nothing,
        and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch
        `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes
        reaches the plan until the user accepts it.

        Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the
        mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story",
        to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing
        story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it. The
        planning prompt of the @{BakedSystemPrompts} asks for each proposal
        as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its
        title, its mode, its target, `new` or the story's id, and its
        prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply says; a
        block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New
        story", with a muted note saying so.

    specGrounding:
        A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written
        from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the
        spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it
        changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component,
        or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as
        every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton
        slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the
        @{ModeSystemPrompts} says, and the planning prompt of the
        @{BakedSystemPrompts} tells it to.

        Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story`
        block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the
        compiled reference heading it comes from, as
        `.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#sprint`, with a short line
        of what in it the story touches, and the story's prompt names those
        elements and links to them, as a prompt written for a mode does, so
        the run it is sent to reads them first. Only elements the drafter
        found are cited: a link must point at a heading that exists in the
        compiled reference, and the application checks each one when the
        proposal arrives, dropping any that doesn't, with a muted note on
        the card saying which link it dropped and why.

        Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for
        something the spec doesn't describe yet, the story says so instead
        of inventing one: its `spec` list holds an entry reading "No match",
        with what was looked for, and its prompt says plainly that the spec
        has nothing on it yet, so the change is new. A proposal with no
        element at all, and no "No match", isn't shown as a story: its card
        says the drafter cited no spec, in the theme's warning colour, with
        "Draft again", which runs the draft for that story once more.

        The citations are shown on the proposal's card, beneath its prompt,
        as a short list, each element's name and section as a link that
        opens the compiled reference there, a "No match" entry muted with a
        small marker, and are kept with the story once it is accepted,
        listed in the open story beneath its steps as "Spec", and shown in
        its row's tooltip. They can be edited with the story, removed, or
        added to by hand from the compiled reference.

        Each citation says what kind of element it is, "Requirement",
        "Behaviour", "Name", or "Section", shown as a small muted label
        before it, and quotes the few words of the spec it rests on, so what
        the story relies on can be checked at a glance. Grounding holds for
        every proposal, however it came: from Draft stories, from research
        that ends with proposals, and from an Ask answer's `suspense-story`
        block, each checked and flagged the same way when it arrives.

    proposalCards:
        Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at
        its top, "New story" in the theme's accent, or, for an addition,
        "Add to this story" where it targets the story the research or draft
        was started from, and "Add to" and the story's title otherwise, in
        the story's own mode's colour, so where it will go is always read
        before anything else on the card; its title,
        its mode pill, and its prompt beneath, clipped at four lines with
        "Read more"; and three buttons along its foot, "Accept", "Edit", and
        "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit
        opens the card's title, prompt, mode, and target in place, the target
        a menu of "New story" and each story, to be changed before it is
        accepted; editing doesn't accept it. Reject removes the card, with a
        short "Undo" in its place for a few seconds.

        Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to
        the plan is: a new story goes into the Backlog, at its end, in its
        mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until
        it is first opened, its spec citations kept with it, whether it was
        accepted on its own card or with "Accept all", and whether it came
        from drafting, research, or an Ask answer. Accepting never adds
        anything to Next sprint, so it never starts a sprint, however Start
        automatically is set; an accepted story reaches a sprint only once it
        is moved to Next sprint, as the sprint says; an addition is added to the named story as a new
        step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the
        story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new
        step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no
        longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and
        the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted
        again. A story already sent can't be added to: its
        proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from
        the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its
        place, "Added to Backlog" or "Added to <story>", with a link that
        opens the story where it is, in the Backlog or its section.

        Ask answers can propose the same way: a `suspense-story` block in an
        answer is shown as a proposal card, with the same Accept, Edit, and
        Reject, its accepting recording it in the plan as above, so a story
        can come out of a conversation without anything written silently.

    research:
        The agent can be asked to research a topic before anything is
        planned or built: "Research", a button beside "Draft stories" on the
        Backlog's heading, and "Research" in an open story's menu, open a
        box labelled "What should be looked into?". Research runs as a
        read-only investigation, a Question run, as the @{Sandbox} says, which
        can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the
        research prompt of the @{BakedSystemPrompts}, which asks for findings,
        not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and
        lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and
        it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its run is shown in
        the drafting panel as drafting's is, its live line of what it is
        reading, a Stop button, and its spinner.

        Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>",
        rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in a Findings
        list beneath the Backlog, newest first, each a row with its topic,
        when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to
        read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that
        story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in
        `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be
        read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

    paused:
        Once research ends, however it ended, planning is paused. While it
        is paused nothing is implemented: Send sprint, the
        ribbon's Send Sprint, and the sprint's Ctrl+Shift+Enter are disabled,
        their tooltips saying planning is paused for review, and no proposal
        from the research is added to the plan by itself. Stories can still
        be written, edited, ordered, and moved, and proposals still accepted
        or rejected one by one, since those only change the plan.

        Nothing of the plan starts while it is paused, not only nothing new:
        a story of Current sprint still waiting in the queue, not yet
        started, is held where it is, as a queued prompt being edited is
        held, as the @{QueueList} says, its row reading "Held for review",
        muted, and its lane waits on it; a story already running when the
        pause began runs on to its end, since stopping it would leave its
        work half done, and the bar says how many are still running. A
        chain's next step, as a story's steps are sent, is held the same
        way. Once the pause ends, by Resume or Approve, what was held goes
        on in its order, as though nothing had stopped it.

        The pause is plain to see: a bar across the top of Planning, in the
        theme's warning colour, with a pause icon, reads "Paused for review",
        names the research it is waiting on, with a link that opens its
        findings, and holds two buttons, "Resume", which ends the pause, and
        "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at
        once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside
        its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is
        paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends;
        nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second
        research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.

        The pause is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, with the research
        it waits on, as soon as it begins, so it is still paused, and still
        shown so, after the project is closed and opened again, the
        application restarted, or the window reloaded, until it is resumed
        or approved.

    keyboard:
        Everything in Planning can be done from the keyboard. Tab moves
        through the section headings' buttons, the rows, and the open
        story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus
        ring. In a list, Up and Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes
        the focused story, A accepts the focused proposal, E edits it, and R rejects it, and Alt+Up
        and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down, across sections as
        dragging does. Ctrl+N adds a story, Ctrl+Enter moves the focused
        story to Next sprint, or to the Backlog from it, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused
        story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and
        Enter. Delete deletes the focused story after a confirmation.
        Escape closes what is open, a menu, a story, or the drafting or
        research panel, one at a time. Every button and control has a label
        a screen reader reads, as its visible text or, for an icon, its
        tooltip, and each shortcut is given in the tooltip of the control it
        stands for.

        Ctrl+Shift+D opens Draft stories and Ctrl+Shift+R opens Research,
        each focusing its box, where Ctrl+Enter starts it; F6 moves focus
        between the column's regions, the pause bar, each section, an open
        panel, and back, so each is a single stop; within the pause bar, Tab
        reaches Resume and Approve and send sprint; within an open story, Tab
        reaches its steps, its Add step, and its Spec citations, each
        citation opening on Enter; and within Findings, Enter opens the
        focused finding in its tab. The Start automatically switch is reached
        by Tab on Next sprint's heading and toggled with Space. Focus never
        lands on something hidden or disabled, and after an action it stays
        where it was or moves to what the action made, as the new story or
        the next proposal, never back to the top.

use /lib
use /ui
from /scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts import ModeSystemPrompts
from /scope/prompt-mode import PromptEditor
from /scope/sandbox import Sandbox
from /scope/prompt-mode/message-list import MessageList
from /scope/application/Body import Body
from /scope/harness-integration/baked-prompts import BakedSystemPrompts
from /scope/project-data import ProjectData
from /scope/prompt-mode/chat-input import ChatInput
from /scope/prompt-mode/modes import PromptModes
from /scope/prompt-mode/queue-list import QueueList
from /scope/prompt-mode/sending import PromptSending
from /ui/behaviours/drag-reorder import DragReorderBehaviour
from /ui/components/growing-text-input import GrowingTextInput

export ui-component Planning:
    pitch:
        A plain, quick list of the work still to do, as Linear keeps issues:
        stories written ahead of time, each saying how it will be sent, Code,
        Chain, Spec, Ask, or Freeform, gathered into the next sprint and sent
        to the agent in order, all at once.

    description:
        Planning opens in a tab of its own in the body, "Planning", with a
        checklist icon, as a file opens, as the @{Body} says, from the
        ribbon's Planning tab or the palette's "Planning". It is one column
        of stories, at most 760 pixels wide, centred, in sections, each
        headed by its name and count: "Current sprint", at the top, only
        while a sprint is under way, then "Next sprint", and "Backlog"
        beneath them. A section with nothing in it reads, muted,
        "Nothing planned" or "Backlog is empty".

    stories:
        A story is one piece of work, written as it will be sent: a title,
        a prompt, and how it will be sent. Each is a row, 36 pixels tall: a
        drag grip at its left; a small mode picker, a pill reading its mode,
        "Code", "Chain", "Spec", "Ask", or "Freeform", in that mode's colour,
        as the @{PromptModes} colours it; its title, in the body's text
        colour, cut off with an ellipsis; then, at its right, muted, a small
        icon for anything attached, and, once it has been sent, its status
        as a task's is shown. Hovering a row shows a menu button at its
        right. A story has no Send of its own, as the sprint says.

        Clicking a row opens it beneath, expanded in place, the others
        moving down: its title, editable in place; its prompt, in a
        @{GrowingTextInput} with the chat input's highlighting, completions,
        and slicing, as the @{ChatInput} has, and its attachments beneath;
        and its parameters, its mode, model, effort, and Slice, as the chat
        input shows them. Every change is saved as it is made. Only one
        story is open at a time; Escape or clicking its row again closes
        it.

    creating:
        Creating a story is quick. A "New story" line at the foot of Next
        sprint, and Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS) while Planning has focus, adds a
        story at the end of Next sprint, open, its title focused, in the mode
        last picked for a story. However a story is added, it goes into Next
        sprint, at its end: a new story, a duplicate, and one added from an
        Ask answer's card with "Add to sprint" alike. It can then be moved to
        the Backlog to wait, as the sprint says. The one exception is an
        accepted proposal for a new story, from drafting, research, or an
        Ask answer's proposal card, which goes into the Backlog, at its end,
        as the proposal cards say, and reaches a sprint only once it is
        moved to Next sprint. Typing a title and pressing Enter adds it and starts another
        beneath it, so a list can be written down without the mouse; Escape
        on an empty one removes it. A title with no prompt sends its title as
        its prompt.

        A story can also be prompted into existence: "Draft stories", a
        button beside the Backlog's heading, opens a small box to say what is
        wanted, in a sentence or a paragraph, and asks the harness, in a run
        of its own with no session, with the planning prompt of the
        @{BakedSystemPrompts}, to break it into stories, each with a title, a
        prompt, and the mode that fits it. They come back as proposals, as
        the drafting and proposals say, each to be accepted, edited, or
        rejected, and none reaches the plan until it is accepted. An Ask
        answer's prompt cards also offer "Add to sprint", which adds the
        card's prompt as a story in its mode to Next sprint.

    sprint:
        Stories move between the Backlog and Next sprint by dragging, as the
        @{DragReorderBehaviour} says, across the sections as within them, or
        from a row's menu, "Move to next sprint" or "Move to backlog". Their
        order within Next sprint is the order they will be sent. A row's menu
        also has "Duplicate" and "Delete".

        "Send sprint", a primary button at the right of Next sprint's
        heading, enabled while it holds a story, sends every story in it, in
        order, as though each had been written in the chat input on its
        mode's tab and sent, one after another, as the @{PromptSending} says:
        each task queues in its lane behind the one before it, in the order
        of the sprint, and each question runs at once. The stories go into
        the queue as one block, so nothing sent later comes between them,
        and the queue's auto-send carries them on as ever, as the
        @{QueueList} says.

        A story can't be sent on its own. The only way a story reaches work
        is through the sprint: a story in the Backlog waits until it is
        moved into Next sprint and the sprint is sent, and a story in Next
        sprint goes when the sprint does. Nothing in Planning, its rows,
        their menus, the open story, the keyboard, the palette, or the
        ribbon, sends a single story, and nothing elsewhere sends a story by
        any other route: a story can't be dragged or copied into the chat
        input or the queue to be sent from there, and its menu has no "Send"
        or "Edit in chat input". The chat input's own prompts are not
        stories and are sent as ever; once a prompt is a story, the sprint is
        its only way to work. To send one story at once, it is the only story in
        Next sprint when Send sprint is pressed. A story that failed or was
        cancelled is sent again the same way, with the next sprint.

        Sending the sprint moves its stories into a "Current sprint" section,
        above Next sprint, shown only while it holds a story, so Next sprint
        is empty again and stories added meanwhile go there, to be the
        sprint after. A story in Current sprint keeps its place, its row
        showing its task's status as it queues, runs, and ends, and clicking
        it opens its task in the Tasks tab; it can't be moved or edited
        there. Once every story of Current sprint has ended, the section
        offers "Close sprint", which moves the stories that are done into a
        muted, collapsed "Done" list beneath the Backlog, and those that
        failed, were cancelled, or stopped to the start of Next sprint, in
        their order, to be sent again. While a sprint is current, Send sprint
        is disabled, its tooltip saying a sprint is already under way.

        Send sprint only ever moves into Current sprint the stories it
        actually sent. A story with nothing to send, its title and its prompt
        both empty, is skipped: it stays in Next sprint, where it was, and
        Send sprint's result says, muted, how many it skipped and why, as "1
        empty story left in Next sprint". A sprint where every story is
        empty sends nothing and makes no Current sprint.

        Once a sprint is done, it can always be closed. Every story of
        Current sprint counts as ended once its task has ended, done,
        failed, cancelled, or stopped, or once its task can no longer be
        found, as when its record was deleted, it was never recorded, or the
        application quit before it was. A story whose task is missing is
        never shown as Queued, or as anything still to come: its row reads
        "Task missing", muted, in the theme's warning colour, its tooltip
        saying its task can't be found, and it counts as ended and not Done.
        A story still waiting in its lane's queue, or held for review, as
        the paused section says, is still to come and hasn't ended. So Close
        sprint shows as soon as no story of Current sprint is building,
        compiling, running, paused, queued, or held, and never waits on a
        task that can't arrive.

        Close sprint treats a story whose task is missing as it treats one
        that failed or was cancelled: it goes back to the start of Next
        sprint, with the others sent again, in their order, never into Done.
        Closing saves the sections, Done, Next sprint, the Backlog, and
        the emptied Current sprint, to `order.json` straight away, as the
        @{ProjectData} says, and Current sprint's state is worked out afresh
        from the stories' tasks whenever the plan is read, so a sprint that
        finished, or whose tasks went missing, before a reload or a restart
        can still be closed after it, as before.

    autoStart:
        Next sprint can start on its own: a "Start automatically" switch on
        Next sprint's heading, beside Send sprint, its tooltip saying the
        next sprint starts as soon as the current one is done. It starts
        off, and is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, so it is kept
        across reloads and restarts.

        While it is on, once every story of Current sprint has ended Done,
        the current sprint closes by itself, as Close sprint closes it, and
        Next sprint, if it holds a story, is sent at once, as Send sprint
        sends it, with nobody having to start it; and while no sprint is
        current, a story added to an empty Next sprint starts it the same
        way. A sprint that ended with a story failed, cancelled, stopped, or with its task missing,
        never starts the next by itself: it waits, Close sprint offered as
        ever, and the switch's row says, in the theme's warning colour, why
        the next didn't start. Nor does the next start while planning is
        paused, as the paused section says: it starts once the pause is
        ended by Resume, or Approve, if the switch is still on. An empty Next
        sprint starts nothing.

        Each time a sprint starts by itself, a passive notification says
        so, "Next sprint started: 4 stories", with a link that opens
        Planning, and the debug log records it. Turning the switch off
        never stops a sprint already sent; it only keeps the next from
        starting by itself. Turning it on while no sprint is current and
        Next sprint holds a story starts Next sprint at once, as adding a
        story to it would, unless planning is paused.

        The switch works while Planning isn't open, from the plan as saved,
        whichever tab is shown. When the project is opened, or the
        application starts, with the switch on, no sprint current, and Next
        sprint holding a story, it doesn't start by itself; the switch's row
        says, muted, "Waiting to start", with a "Start now" button, so a
        sprint never begins unseen as the application opens. A current
        sprint whose stories were cut off when the application quit, as
        every run is, ended them, and never starts the next by itself.

        While the switch is on, Next sprint's heading shows "Auto" beside
        its count, in the theme's accent, and the ribbon's Send Sprint
        button's tooltip says the next sprint starts automatically.

    saving:
        The stories, their order, and which section each is in are saved
        with the project's data, as the @{ProjectData} says, in
        `.suspense/planning/`, a file per story, holding its hidden anchor
        as a queued prompt's is, and an `order.json` listing the sections and
        their stories, so the plan is kept with the project and comes back
        as it was left. A story's steps are saved in its own file, in their
        order, as its steps say, never apart from it.

    steps:
        A story can have steps: one or more further prompts, each a piece of
        the story done after the one before, as a chain's steps are. Each
        step has a prompt, a mode of its own, Code or Spec, starting as the
        story's, and a model and effort, starting as the story's, and may
        have attachments. A story with no steps is just its own prompt, as
        before; its prompt is always its first step.

        An open story lists its steps beneath its prompt, in order, each a
        row numbered from 2, the story's own prompt being 1, with its mode
        pill and the first line of its prompt, opening in place to edit, as
        a story does. "Add step", beneath the last, adds one at the end,
        open and focused; several can be added one after another, Enter in
        an empty step's prompt adding none. Steps are reordered by dragging,
        as the @{DragReorderBehaviour} says, or Alt+Up and Alt+Down, and each
        has a remove button in its row and in its menu. The story's own
        prompt stays first and can't be moved among them.

        A step belongs to its story and to nothing else. It is saved in the
        story's file, in a `steps` list of the story's hidden anchor, in its
        order, and saved as every change to the plan is, straight away; a
        story duplicated copies its steps, and one deleted deletes them. Its
        order is kept wherever the story goes, between sections, into a
        sprint, and back from Done.

        Wherever the story is shown, its steps are too: its row in Planning
        shows how many after its title, muted, as "3 steps", with the list in
        its tooltip; the open story lists them as above; a proposal to add
        to it shows them, so what it would add to can be seen; and once it
        is sent, it is sent as a chain, its prompt first and each step after
        it in order, each step sent only once the one before it finishes, as
        the @{PromptEditor}'s chained tasks are, so the Tasks tab shows the
        story as one chain with its steps beneath it. A story sent can't be
        given more steps; its steps, sent or still to come, read as they
        were sent. In Current sprint, a story with steps is expanded, a row
        for each step beneath it, in order, indented 16 pixels, each with its
        own status, as a running chain's are in the Tasks tab; in Done, and
        in a finding started from the story, its steps are listed the same
        way, collapsed to its step count until it is expanded. The same steps,
        in the same order, are what every place shows, since every place
        reads them from the story's own file.

        A step is only ever added to a story that exists. Adding one to a
        story that doesn't, as one deleted while a proposal naming it waited,
        or by another window, or whose file was removed from
        `.suspense/planning/` meanwhile, changes nothing: no story is made
        for it, no other story is given it, and nothing is saved. It says so
        in plain words where it was asked for, as "That story no longer
        exists, so the step wasn't added", in the theme's error colour, as
        the states say, with what was to be added kept, so it can be added
        to another story or as a new one. A step added to a story already
        sent is refused the same way, saying the story has been sent.

    layout:
        Everything in Planning is laid out on one rhythm, so it scans as a
        single list. The column has 24 pixels of padding at its top and
        sides. Each section's heading is a row 32 pixels tall: its name in
        small semibold text, its count beside it, muted, and its actions at
        its right, each a labelled button, never an icon alone; 8 pixels
        beneath it its first row. Story rows are 36 pixels tall, 2 pixels
        apart, each with 12 pixels of padding at either side, their parts in
        fixed columns, so the grips, mode pills, titles, and statuses line up
        down the whole list: the grip 16 pixels, the mode pill 72 pixels, the
        title the rest, the status and time right-aligned in a column of
        their own 96 pixels wide, then the row's buttons. Sections are 24
        pixels apart. Every row's state reads the same way, as below, and
        every label is the same small text, muted where it is secondary.

        From top to bottom, Planning reads: the pause bar, while paused;
        Current sprint, while a sprint is under way; Next sprint; Backlog;
        Findings; and Done, collapsed. Each is a section headed as above, so
        nothing sits outside the rhythm, and an open story, a drafting or
        research panel, and the citations and steps inside a story all use
        the same three parts, below.

    parts:
        Everything in Planning is built from three parts, each always drawn
        the same way:

        \\
        - A row: 36 pixels tall, in the fixed columns above, for stories, steps, findings, and Done; its secondary text muted and cut off with an ellipsis, its buttons small ghost buttons with labels, shown at its right on hover and always while it is focused
        - A panel: an inset area 16 pixels below what opened it, on the theme's raised surface, corners rounded 6 pixels, 12 pixels of padding, a heading row of 32 pixels with its name, as "Draft stories", "Research", or the story's title, and its close button, its content beneath, and its actions in a footer row, right-aligned, the primary action last; used for an open story, drafting, and research
        - A card: a box inside a panel, on the theme's base surface, with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour, corners rounded 4 pixels, 12 pixels of padding, 8 pixels from the next; a label row at its top, its content, and a footer row of labelled buttons; used for proposals and for each finding's summary
        \\

        Labels are words, never icons alone: every button reads what it
        does, "Accept", "Send sprint", "Start automatically", and an icon
        beside a label only repeats it. Each heading's count is a plain
        number, muted, and each status a coloured label, as the states say.
        The pause bar is a row across the column's top, 40 pixels tall, its
        text and buttons on one line, the same height whatever it says.

    states:
        Each part of Planning has the same few states, shown the same way
        wherever they come up, so a state is never guessed from what is
        missing.

        \\
        - Empty: a single muted line, centred in the section, saying what is missing and what to do, as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N.", with no illustration
        - Loading: a spinner and a short muted label of what is happening, as "Drafting stories…", in the place the result will appear, never a blank space
        - Paused: a story whose task is paused shows "Paused" as its status, in the theme's warning colour, with a small pause icon, and a "Resume" button in its row, as the PromptSending says of pausing; a sprint with any story paused says so in its heading, as "1 paused", in the same colour
        - Error: a line in the theme's error colour, saying what went wrong in plain words, with what the harness or the application reported beneath it collapsed under "Details", and a "Try again" button where trying again can help
        \\

        A story's status in its row is the same coloured label a task has,
        as the @{MessageList}'s status says, Queued, Running with its spinner
        and time, Done, Failed, Cancelled, Paused, or, where its task can't be found, Task missing, as the sprint says, and a story not yet
        sent shows nothing there, so its absence means "not sent".

        Each part shows each state that can come up for it, worded for it:

        \\
        - Story list: empty, "Nothing planned. Press Ctrl+N to add a story." in Next sprint and "Nothing waiting." in the Backlog; loading, while the plan is read on opening, a row of skeleton rows, never an empty section; error, when the plan can't be read or saved, saying which file and why, with "Try again"
        - Research and its findings: loading, the live line of what it is reading with its spinner; empty, "No findings yet." in Findings; error, the run's failure with "Try again", which keeps the question in its box; a finding that ended early, as stopped, marked "Incomplete", muted, in its row
        - Pause: the pause bar, in the theme's warning colour, as the paused section says, and the sprint's Send buttons disabled with their tooltips saying why; a sprint that can't start for a failed story says so in its heading, in the same colour
        - Proposals: loading, the drafting line and spinner; empty, "No stories proposed." with "Draft again"; error, the run's failure with "Try again"; a proposal with no spec cited, in the warning colour with "Draft again", as the spec grounding says
        \\

    drafting:
        Drafting stories shows its work in one place, a panel opened beneath
        the Backlog's heading, never in a popup that hides the list. It has
        the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and
        beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what
        the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner,
        updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel
        lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all"
        buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left
        to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and
        leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing
        says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided,
        so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.

        Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent"
        in its row's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then
        reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's
        title and prompt, and the panel opens beneath that story rather than
        the Backlog's heading.

    proposals:
        The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run,
        as the @{Sandbox} says, able to read the project and change nothing,
        and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch
        `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes
        reaches the plan until the user accepts it.

        Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the
        mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story",
        to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing
        story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it. The
        planning prompt of the @{BakedSystemPrompts} asks for each proposal
        as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its
        title, its mode, its target, `new` or the story's id, and its
        prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply says; a
        block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New
        story", with a muted note saying so.

    specGrounding:
        A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written
        from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the
        spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it
        changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component,
        or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as
        every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton
        slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the
        @{ModeSystemPrompts} says, and the planning prompt of the
        @{BakedSystemPrompts} tells it to.

        Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story`
        block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the
        element in the spec's Piton source, under the spec location, never
        to the compiled reference: the .pi file, relative to the project
        directory, then `#` and the element it names, an anchor or a
        property on one, in the form `piton slice` takes, as
        `spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint`, with a short line of
        what in it the story touches. The story's prompt names those
        elements and links to them in the same form. Only elements the
        drafter found are cited, and where they point is the only thing
        that is Piton source: the drafter still learns what the spec says
        only from the compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints,
        never by reading the Piton source, as the @{ModeSystemPrompts} says,
        and works out each element's source from what `piton slice` prints
        for it, which names the file each declaration is in.

        The application checks each link against the Piton source when the
        proposal arrives: the file has to exist under the spec location, and
        has to define the named element, the anchor declared in it and, for
        a property, that property on it, as `piton slice` would find it. A
        link that fails either check is dropped, with a muted note on the
        card saying which link it dropped and why, "no such file" or "the
        file doesn't define Planning.sprint". Each citation, on the proposal
        card and in an accepted story's "Spec" list, opens that place in the
        Piton source, the file in the editor at the element's declaration,
        as the OpenFile opens a file.

        Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for
        something the spec doesn't describe yet, the story says so instead
        of inventing one: its `spec` list holds an entry reading "No match",
        with what was looked for, and its prompt says plainly that the spec
        has nothing on it yet, so the change is new. A proposal with no
        element at all, and no "No match", isn't shown as a story: its card
        says the drafter cited no spec, in the theme's warning colour, with
        "Draft again", which runs the draft for that story once more.

        The citations are shown on the proposal's card, beneath its prompt,
        as a short list, each element's name and section as a link that
        opens the compiled reference there, a "No match" entry muted with a
        small marker, and are kept with the story once it is accepted,
        listed in the open story beneath its steps as "Spec", and shown in
        its row's tooltip. They can be edited with the story, removed, or
        added to by hand from the compiled reference.

        Each citation says what kind of element it is, "Requirement",
        "Behaviour", "Name", or "Section", shown as a small muted label
        before it, and quotes the few words of the spec it rests on, so what
        the story relies on can be checked at a glance. Grounding holds for
        every proposal, however it came: from Draft stories, from research
        that ends with proposals, and from an Ask answer's `suspense-story`
        block, each checked and flagged the same way when it arrives.

    proposalCards:
        Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at
        its top, "New story" in the theme's accent, or, for an addition,
        "Add to this story" where it targets the story the research or draft
        was started from, and "Add to" and the story's title otherwise, in
        the story's own mode's colour, so where it will go is always read
        before anything else on the card; its title,
        its mode pill, and its prompt beneath, clipped at four lines with
        "Read more"; and three buttons along its foot, "Accept", "Edit", and
        "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit
        opens the card's title, prompt, mode, and target in place, the target
        a menu of "New story" and each story, to be changed before it is
        accepted; editing doesn't accept it. Reject removes the card, with a
        short "Undo" in its place for a few seconds.

        Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to
        the plan is: a new story goes into the Backlog, at its end, in its
        mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until
        it is first opened, its spec citations kept with it, whether it was
        accepted on its own card or with "Accept all", and whether it came
        from drafting, research, or an Ask answer. Accepting never adds
        anything to Next sprint, so it never starts a sprint, however Start
        automatically is set; an accepted story reaches a sprint only once it
        is moved to Next sprint, as the sprint says; an addition is added to the named story as a new
        step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the
        story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new
        step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no
        longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and
        the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted
        again. A story already sent can't be added to: its
        proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from
        the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its
        place, "Added to Backlog" or "Added to <story>", with a link that
        opens the story where it is, in the Backlog or its section.

        Ask answers can propose the same way: a `suspense-story` block in an
        answer is shown as a proposal card, with the same Accept, Edit, and
        Reject, its accepting recording it in the plan as above, so a story
        can come out of a conversation without anything written silently.

    research:
        The agent can be asked to research a topic before anything is
        planned or built: "Research", a button beside "Draft stories" on the
        Backlog's heading, and "Research" in an open story's menu, open a
        box labelled "What should be looked into?". Research runs as a
        read-only investigation, a Question run, as the @{Sandbox} says, which
        can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the
        research prompt of the @{BakedSystemPrompts}, which asks for findings,
        not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and
        lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and
        it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its run is shown in
        the drafting panel as drafting's is, its live line of what it is
        reading, a Stop button, and its spinner.

        Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>",
        rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in a Findings
        list beneath the Backlog, newest first, each a row with its topic,
        when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to
        read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that
        story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in
        `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be
        read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

    paused:
        Once research ends, however it ended, planning is paused. While it
        is paused nothing is implemented: Send sprint, the
        ribbon's Send Sprint, and the sprint's Ctrl+Shift+Enter are disabled,
        their tooltips saying planning is paused for review, and no proposal
        from the research is added to the plan by itself. Stories can still
        be written, edited, ordered, and moved, and proposals still accepted
        or rejected one by one, since those only change the plan.

        Nothing of the plan starts while it is paused, not only nothing new:
        a story of Current sprint still waiting in the queue, not yet
        started, is held where it is, as a queued prompt being edited is
        held, as the @{QueueList} says, its row reading "Held for review",
        muted, and its lane waits on it; a story already running when the
        pause began runs on to its end, since stopping it would leave its
        work half done, and the bar says how many are still running. A
        chain's next step, as a story's steps are sent, is held the same
        way. Once the pause ends, by Resume or Approve, what was held goes
        on in its order, as though nothing had stopped it.

        The pause is plain to see: a bar across the top of Planning, in the
        theme's warning colour, with a pause icon, reads "Paused for review",
        names the research it is waiting on, with a link that opens its
        findings, and holds two buttons, "Resume", which ends the pause, and
        "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at
        once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside
        its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is
        paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends;
        nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second
        research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.

        The pause is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, with the research
        it waits on, as soon as it begins, so it is still paused, and still
        shown so, after the project is closed and opened again, the
        application restarted, or the window reloaded, until it is resumed
        or approved.

    keyboard:
        Everything in Planning can be done from the keyboard. Tab moves
        through the section headings' buttons, the rows, and the open
        story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus
        ring. In a list, Up and Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes
        the focused story, A accepts the focused proposal, E edits it, and R rejects it, and Alt+Up
        and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down, across sections as
        dragging does. Ctrl+N adds a story, Ctrl+Enter moves the focused
        story to Next sprint, or to the Backlog from it, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused
        story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and
        Enter. Delete deletes the focused story after a confirmation.
        Escape closes what is open, a menu, a story, or the drafting or
        research panel, one at a time. Every button and control has a label
        a screen reader reads, as its visible text or, for an icon, its
        tooltip, and each shortcut is given in the tooltip of the control it
        stands for.

        Ctrl+Shift+D opens Draft stories and Ctrl+Shift+R opens Research,
        each focusing its box, where Ctrl+Enter starts it; F6 moves focus
        between the column's regions, the pause bar, each section, an open
        panel, and back, so each is a single stop; within the pause bar, Tab
        reaches Resume and Approve and send sprint; within an open story, Tab
        reaches its steps, its Add step, and its Spec citations, each
        citation opening on Enter; and within Findings, Enter opens the
        focused finding in its tab. The Start automatically switch is reached
        by Tab on Next sprint's heading and toggled with Space. Focus never
        lands on something hidden or disabled, and after an action it stays
        where it was or moves to what the action made, as the new story or
        the next proposal, never back to the top.
